minutes.headline: Committee voted that ARPA/Esser funds now in the budget must revert to the town if the property-tax override passes
minutes.summary: This was a long, wide-ranging remote School Committee meeting: routine business (minutes, warrants, a surplus truck, staff-appreciation resolutions, an eclipse-glasses donation) alongside substantive discussion of the pending override and the superintendent's evaluation timeline. The committee voted 5-0 that if the override passes, one-time ARPA/Esser funds currently built into the level-service budget should revert to the select board rather than be kept by the schools, while agreeing to ask for some of it back for facilities needs like HVAC repairs; members also discussed an AT&T cell tower revenue opportunity and committed to building a public communication explaining what the override is (and is not) for.

what_happened.line: The committee voted 5-0 that one-time ARPA/Esser funds built into the level-service budget should revert to the town if the property-tax override passes.
Members disputed where the original override figure came from and whether it includes money beyond the gap between two budget versions.
The committee agreed to let the facilities director keep exploring a possible AT&T cell tower on district property as a revenue source.
A public document explaining what the override does and does not fund will be developed and discussed at the next meeting.
The superintendent evaluation timeline was set, with draft materials due June 5th and discussion at the June 19th meeting.

why_it_matters: Voters deciding the override should know one-time federal relief funds now inside the school budget would leave the schools, not stay as ongoing capacity, if the override passes.
The disputed origin of the override figure means residents may be voting on a number the committee itself could not fully explain the basis for.
A cell tower lease and the promised explainer document are both potential future revenue or clarity for taxpayers evaluating the override.
watch_next: Next School Committee meeting: the public override-explainer document

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every vote, on the AT&T cell tower decision, and on future-topics; nearly all the divergence is that the official minutes narrate the override/facilities discussion in prose without repeating the dollar figures, percentages and debt-schedule numbers that were spoken aloud and that our minutes captured from the recording. The one place a reader should actually check something is the "bagged lunches" line, where our caption-derived $7 and the official's "available for 7 p.m." describe the same moment two different ways.
